items.title: Arcane: Environment access token bypasses the admin-required authorization gate on `/api/debug/pprof`
items.summary: ## Summary Arcane v2.10.2 contains an authorization inconsistency in `AuthMiddleware.managerAuth`. items.title: lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects
items.summary: `lopdf::Document::load_mem` (and the other `load*` entry points) parses nested PDF arrays and dictionaries with unbounded recursion. A small crafted PDF whose Catalog contains a deeply nested array (`/X [[[ … ]]]`, on the order of 10,000 levels) exhausts the call stack and aborts the process with `SIGABRT`. Because this is a stack-overflow abort rather than a `panic!`, it cannot be caught with `catch_unwind`: any service that parses untrusted PDF input with lopdf can be crashed by a ~21 KB file,

items.summary: ### Summary `IPCameraFrameGrabber` parses the `Content-Length` value from the multipart MJPEG HTTP stream returned by the configured IP camera without any bounds checking. items.title: Claude Agent SDK: Argument Injection via resume Option Allows Arbitrary Command Execution
items.summary: The Claude Agent SDK for Python passed the `resume` option to the Claude CLI without validation, allowing a value beginning with `-` to be interpreted as a separate CLI flag. An attacker who controlled the `resume` value could inject an `--mcp-config` flag defining a stdio MCP server, resulting in arbitrary command execution at CLI startup that bypassed the SDK's permission controls. items.title: ckan-mcp-server: DataStore Table UI resource does not validate postMessage origin (in) and posts to targetOrigin "*" (out)
items.summary: ## Summary The MCP Apps UI resource (an interactive DataStore table rendered in the host's webview/iframe) communicates with its parent via `postMessage`. Its inbound `message` listener performs no `event.origin` validation, and its outbound messages are sent with target origin `'*'`. items.title: swoosh has email-derived URL path injection in Microsoft Graph endpoint
items.summary: ### Summary `Swoosh.Adapters.MsGraph` builds its Microsoft Graph API request URL by interpolating the sender's email address directly into the URL path (`/users/{from}/sendMail`) without percent-encoding or validation. In applications that derive the `from` address from untrusted or user-influenced input (a relay, a contact form, or a "send as" feature), an attacker can inject URL-special characters into the local part of the address to escape the intended path segment and rewrite the request's

items.title: ClickMigrate has Path Traversal in "revision -m" argument
items.summary: ### Impact A path traversal vulnerability in the `revision` command allowed a crafted migration name supplied via the `-m` argument to escape the intended migrations directory. Under specific conditions, an attacker could cause the tool to create a `.sql` file in an arbitrary location writable by the user executing the command. This issue is only exploitable if an attacker can influence the migration name passed to the `revision` command, such as through an insecure automation or CI/CD pipeline

items.title: gomarkdown/markdown IsSafeURL panics on short URLs
